title: Admin Ops Assembler: catalyst for runbooks-as-tasks and lightweight admin utilities
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create an 'Assembler' service and developer ergonomics layer that converts existing runbooks and admin scripts into composable, permissioned tasks (actionlets). Goal is to reduce mean-time-to-remediate (MTTR) for common support flows, enable safe self-service for first-line engineers, and provide strong telemetry/approval hooks for escalations.
acceptance_criteria: Can register a runbook fragment and expose it as an actionlet with typed inputs and metadata
Actionlets execute within a permissioned sandbox, honoring RBAC and audit log requirements
Console shows per-actionlet latency/cost and per-invocation telemetry (requester, inputs, outcome)
Support team can create a new actionlet from an existing runbook in under 60 minutes using the assembler UI
Rollout supports canary gating to a single support cohort and automatic rollback on failure signatures
implementation_notes: We will implement a lightweight registry that stores actionlet manifests (YAML) and maps to execution adapters (Kubernetes Job, ephemeral container, or serverless task)
Prefer idempotent step design: actionlets must safely run multiple times or detect previous completion (idempotency keys)
Telemetry will reuse existing tracing headers and extend the ops telemetry schema with actionlet.name and actionlet.version
Decision: start with a delegated-exec model (control-plane holds metadata; ephemeral worker runs with scoped short-lived credentials) to avoid shipping credential material in the registry
Trade-off: delegated-exec increases coordination complexity but significantly reduces blast radius compared with running everything in the control plane
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): internal alpha with 3 curated actionlets (clear cache, refresh model artifacts, collect kube-pod-logs) - target: SRE + 2 support engineers
Phase 2 (beta): open registrar for 10 support recipes, add RBAC templates and approval hooks; run weekly review meetings
Phase 3 (ga): promote to console catalog, wire cost/latency dashboards and SLO monitoring; provide onboarding doc and CI validations
risks: Privilege escalation if worker credentials are mis-scoped - mitigated by least-privilege templates and HSM-backed short token issuance
Incorrect idempotency assumptions leading to destructive retries - mitigated by static analyzers and post-deploy smoke tests
Operational load from users creating too many low-quality actionlets - mitigated by quota + review + templates
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and input schema validation
Integration test harness that spins ephemeral workers in staging and validates audit logs and RBAC enforcement
Chaos test: random worker termination during actionlet execution to ensure retry/backoff semantics preserve consistency
Load test: simulate 200 concurrent short actionlets to validate autoscaling and queueing behavior
